original_question: Determine whether classical Maxwell electrodynamics can provide a description of quantum spin and whether there is a principled relationship among spin, the Aharonov effect, and hidden-variable interpretations of quantum mechanics.
target_in_paper: Section 6, introductory "Questions" (I) and (II) in "Origin of Spin: Paradox of the classical Beth experiment."
correct_elements: The draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the two explicit questions posed at the start of Section 6: whether classical Maxwell electrodynamics can describe quantum spin, and whether there is a linkage between spin, the Aharonov effect, and hidden-variable interpretations of quantum mechanics.
missing_details: The paper frames these questions specifically through the Beth experiment paradox: a birefringent plate experiences torque although, in the doubled-beam setup, the Poynting/energy flux is claimed to vanish.
The nearby context says the paradox is to be addressed by introducing a nonzero classical electromagnetic spin tensor; the draft omits this concrete mechanism.
The paper’s wording is "Is there plausible linkage..." rather than a stronger formulation such as "principled relationship."
The scope is Section 6’s classical-electrodynamics discussion, not a broad inquiry into all possible classical models of spin.
The immediate paper-faithful reformulation should mention that the proposed explanation treats the observed torque as spin flux rather than orbital angular-momentum flux.
The section contrasts the proposal with standard classical electrodynamics, where the usual spin tensor is taken to be zero; this contrast is omitted in the draft.
No ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier conditions appear here; this is a conceptual electrodynamics question, not an algebraic one.
refined_question: In Beth’s classical circularly polarized-light / birefringent-plate experiment, where the doubled-beam setup is claimed to exert a torque on the plate despite vanishing Poynting (energy-flux) transfer, can classical Maxwell electrodynamics be supplemented by a nonzero electromagnetic spin tensor so that the torque is explained as spin flux and thereby provide a classical electromagnetic description of quantum spin; and, within that same spin-based framework, is there a plausible linkage between spin, the Aharonov effect, and hidden-variable interpretations of quantum mechanics?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 6 rather than any other part of the paper: its two clauses are essentially a paraphrase of Questions (I) and (II) printed at the opening of "Origin of Spin: Paradox of the classical Beth experiment." The immediately surrounding text narrows the intended scope to Beth’s experiment and says the paradox can be removed by introducing a classical spin tensor. Sections 6.2-6.4 then provide the concrete nearby context: the Beth setup is presented as a torque-without-Poynting-flux puzzle, and the proposed resolution is to add a spin term to the electromagnetic angular-momentum balance and interpret the torque as spin flux. By contrast, the Aharonov/hidden-variable part is only posed as a question and not developed into a theorem or equivalent reformulation, so the refined question should preserve that open-ended status and the paper’s weaker wording of "plausible linkage."
